facts.title: A Key Developmental Gene Is Named After Sonic the Hedgehog
facts.summary: A gene that helps build limbs, fingers and the brain in vertebrates is called sonic hedgehog, after the video game character Sonic the Hedgehog.

facts.title: All Wild Hedgehogs Can Hibernate
facts.summary: All wild hedgehogs can hibernate, though how long they stay dormant depends on the temperature, the species and how much food is available.

facts.title: Baby Hedgehogs Are Born With Their Spines Hidden Under Fluid
facts.summary: Baby hedgehogs, called hoglets, are born with spines already in place, but buried under a pocket of fluid-filled tissue.

facts.title: Drug-Resistant MRSA Evolved on Hedgehogs Before Antibiotics Existed
facts.summary: A type of MRSA, the drug-resistant superbug, appears to have evolved on hedgehogs long before humans began using antibiotics in medicine.

facts.title: Europe's Garden Hedgehog Became Near Threatened in 2024
facts.summary: In October 2024, the Western European hedgehog, the familiar garden hedgehog, was moved from Least Concern to Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

facts.title: Hedgehog Spines Are Hollow Hairs
facts.summary: A hedgehog's spines are hollow hairs made stiff with keratin, the same tough protein found in human fingernails.

facts.title: Hedgehog Spines Don't Fall Out Like Porcupine Quills
facts.summary: Unlike porcupine quills, hedgehog spines are not barbed or poisonous and do not easily come loose from the body.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Are Lactose Intolerant, So Milk Is Bad for Them
facts.summary: Despite the old picture of a hedgehog lapping from a saucer, hedgehogs are lactose intolerant, and wildlife charities ask people not to leave milk out for them.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Are Named After Hedges and Pigs
facts.summary: The name hedgehog came into use around 1450.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Are Surprisingly Noisy
facts.summary: Hedgehogs are far from silent animals.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Can Roam 1 to 2 Kilometres in a Single Night
facts.summary: A hedgehog can travel an average of 1 to 2 kilometres in a single night, and sometimes more, as it moves between feeding spots in the dark.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Have Barely Changed in 15 Million Years
facts.summary: Hedgehogs have changed little over the last 15 million years, keeping much the same spiny body plan throughout that time.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Have Some Resistance to Snake Venom
facts.summary: Hedgehogs have some natural resistance to snake venom, thanks partly to a protein called erinacin in their muscles.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Roll Into a Ball for Protection
facts.summary: When threatened, a hedgehog rolls into a tight spiny ball, tucking its furry face, feet and belly inside so that only spines face the attacker.

facts.title: Hedgehogs Smear Foamy Spit on Their Spines
facts.summary: When a hedgehog encounters a new scent, it may lick and bite the source, whip up a scented froth in its mouth and paste it onto its spines with its tongue.

facts.title: In New Zealand, Hedgehogs Are an Invasive Predator
facts.summary: In Britain the hedgehog is a declining garden favourite, but in New Zealand it is an introduced predator that threatens native wildlife.

facts.title: No Hedgehogs Are Native to the Americas or Australia
facts.summary: No living hedgehog species is native to the Americas or to Australia.

facts.title: There Are 17 Species of Hedgehog
facts.summary: There are 17 species of hedgehog, grouped into five genera.
